title: Cursor: Git at any scale — publication and rebuildable replicas
objective: Make Git updates authoritative through an object-store publication index, recover interrupted operations, and serve reads from verifiably caught-up, rebuildable replicas.

lessons.title: Having the objects is not having the update
lessons.outcome: Import a supplied pack without moving a branch; compare cat-file with show-ref, then conditionally move the ref. Identify the separate payload and visibility boundaries.

lessons.title: Upload first, publish second
lessons.outcome: Stop after uploading a payload but before publishing its index entry. Observe an unreferenced object and an unchanged authoritative head; publish it and identify the acknowledgement boundary.

lessons.title: Two writers, one publication order
lessons.outcome: Race two writers using the same index ETag. Observe one winner and one conditional failure; refresh and revalidate the loser, distinguishing a retryable index conflict from a rejected stale branch update.

lessons.title: The publish succeeded; the reply disappeared
lessons.outcome: Suppress the publisher's success reply after index publication. Reconcile a stable operation ID against the published history and retry without adding a second logical update; compare with an unpublished upload.

lessons.title: Turn published history into a Git replica
lessons.outcome: Materialize an empty bare repository from the ordered published entries. Compare refs and reachable objects with the expected head; deliberately omit a required pack and observe replay stop before advancing its applied position.

lessons.title: Crash between applying a ref and recording progress
lessons.outcome: Stop the replayer after a ref update but before its applied marker. Restart and inspect the old/new ref comparison: the repeated entry is recognized, a divergent ref is rejected, and progress never runs ahead of Git state.

lessons.title: Lose a notification without serving a stale read
lessons.outcome: Pause replica catch-up and drop its wake-up, then compare a direct stale read with a read guarded by an index check. Observe catch-up before serving and a bounded failure when the authority cannot be checked.

lessons.title: Scale a repository down to zero warm copies
lessons.outcome: Remove all disposable local Git copies while retaining the object store, then reconstruct two replicas from published history. Verify refs, reachable content and fsck; measure cold versus warm work and show that a missing published object prevents a complete rebuild.
